physical_properties_notes: EQ Cet = 1RXS J012851.9-233931 / RBS0206 is a low-accretion-rate polar. Schwope+99 identify the optical counterpart and report likely orbital periods around 90 min (0.0625 d) or 146 min (0.1 d), with the shorter period favored but not conclusive from the short photometric baseline; the catalog value 1.5469 h is close to the ~90 min solution. Their low-state spectrum is dominated by the magnetic WD, with no obvious mass-donating-secondary feature. The absence of an M-star feature gives d>240 pc if an M6/Gl406 Roche-lobe-filling donor at Porb~90 min contributes at most 80 percent near 9000 A; this is a distance/donor assumption, not a measured donor spectral type, mass, or temperature. WD-atmosphere scaling assumes Mwd=0.6 Msun and Rwd=8e8 cm: a 10000 K WD fits the blue flux at 130 pc but has too steep a slope, while a 20000 K WD is required at 240 pc and gives a worse continuum fit, so phase-resolved data were requested. Zeeman absorption gives a mean photospheric field B=36 +/-1 MG; under dipole/homogeneous-temperature assumptions the polar field is likely 55-60 MG with a lower limit around 40 MG. The single cyclotron hump gives accretion-region B=45 +/-1 MG and plasma temperature kT<2 keV. Barrett+20 radio-inferred 7530 +/-365 G is an emission-region estimate and should not be mixed with the MG WD/accretion-field measurements. Follow-up Schwope+02_RBS resolves the earlier 90/146-min ambiguity for the stable polarimetric modulation: P=92.815 +/- 0.003 min is the WD spin period and is likely the orbit; high-state H-alpha gives 96 +/- 4 min with K=125 km/s, but the authors attribute much of the line emission to the channeled stream, so this is not a donor dynamical mass constraint. Source was high-state in Dec. 2000 and has documented low state (1998) / high-state variability; Breedt+12 explicitly removes it from the pre-polar category. Schwope+02_RBS high-state cyclotron spectra are a two-component/two-spot modeling problem (32 MG, kT=10 keV spot 2 and persistent low-state 45 MG component), with a 33.7 MG alternate low-temperature fit to the 8000-A hump; no firm accretion geometry. Campbell+08 abstract adds a phase-resolved IR fit (34 MG, kT=3.5 keV, log Lambda=4.1), but the full article/table was inaccessible. Gaia DR3 phot_variable_flag=VARIABLE; its BP/RP/G measurements are unresolved system photometry and must not be read as component magnitudes or WD Teff. No source-specific extinction estimate was retained. Cas 1 = RX J0153.3+7446 = 1RXS J015317.9+744641 = Gaia DR3 558935743846455296. SIMBAD exact alias lookup, original optical identification, and Gaia source-ID query support the counterpart. CV identification is secure from the emission-line spectrum; whether it is magnetic/IP remains disputed. Haberl & Motch (1995) proposed an IP but explicitly said its 1414 s ROSAT modulation was less evident and required confirmation. Norton et al. (2006) favored 1974 +/- 30 s as WD spin and 2333 +/- 5 s as an optical beat/sideband, but RXTE data did not confirm coherent periods. Bruch (2025) says IP status is not established beyond doubt and reports only a separate 3486.09(68) s TESS signal of unknown origin. An ARIES seminar abstract (2026-05-12) calls Cas 1 definitively non-magnetic from optical spectra, but underlying paper/spectra were not available. Therefore inherited broad class magnetic_cv is retained for compatibility while subclass is marked disputed; do not use it as a confirmed magnetic CV in population comparisons.

Gaia DR3 astrometry is ICRS at J2016.0; J2000 coordinates are propagated ICRS, not FK5/J2000. The exact source has RUWE=1.014, 21 visibility periods, astrometric_params_solved=31, phot_variable_flag=VARIABLE, and BP/RP excess 1.3346. Gaia colors/magnitudes are unresolved system photometry. The Bailer-Jones geometric distance is 1367.0 pc with 16th/84th percentiles 1279.8/1474.4 pc; the photogeometric estimate is 1361.5 pc (+85.7/-73.4 pc). Barrett et al. (2020) list 1608 pc from Gaia DR2; retain it as an older competing estimate. No source-specific extinction estimate was found, so no intrinsic color is adopted. Absolute G values in the ledger are derived unresolved-system values without extinction correction.

Thorstensen et al. (2017) Table 1 provides the spectroscopic orbital period 0.16415(1) d = 3.9396(24) h from emission-line radial velocities. Haberl & Motch (1995) Fig. 1 reports a 1414 s ROSAT modulation. Norton et al. (2006) reanalyzed the sparse 1992 ROSAT photons: 1974 +/-30 s is their preferred, still candidate WD-spin alias; they report optical 2333 +/-5 s, interpreted conditionally as a beat/sideband. Butters et al. (2011) found no significant RXTE periodicity at either period; Bruch (2025) did not recover earlier periods in four noisy TESS light curves. Bruch's single 3486.09(68) s signal has unidentified origin. A local consistency calculation using 1974 s and the spectroscopic orbit predicts beat period 2293.2 +/-40.5 s (independent 1-sigma propagation), compatible with 2333 +/-5 s only within the broad spin-alias uncertainty; this does not resolve the clock identification.

Haberl & Motch Table 2 fixes a bremsstrahlung temperature at 10 keV and gives 0.1-2.4 keV flux 3.4e-13 erg cm-2 s-1; the table does not specify whether this flux is absorbed or unabsorbed. Fitted NH=32(+30/-19)e20 cm-2 with 90% confidence for two parameters; reduced chi-square 2.7. Do not propagate this flux into broader X-ray catalog bands. Norton et al. estimate magnetic moment ~6e33 G cm3 under spin-equilibrium assumptions; this is not a measured field. Barrett et al. report C-band Stokes I=21 +/-10 uJy with circular polarization -100 +/-39%; Ridder et al. later exclude it from their luminosity plot because it is below 3 sigma. The reported 1960 +/-365 G is inferred under fundamental electron-cyclotron-maser emission from a presumed donor corona; it is neither a WD surface field nor a secure detection. Exact C-band edges are 4.464-6.512 GHz; observing epoch/state is not specified in the paper. No WD Teff, mass, radius, log g, cooling age, direct WD field, donor spectral type/mass/temperature/radius, mass ratio, inclination, period derivative, accretion rate/state, or Roche-filling measurement was found in the searched source-specific literature.

Coppejans+16 give Porb=0.209893(1) d from Kaitchuck+89, a K5+/-2 secondary from Knigge+06, no prior radio detections, and VLA 8-12 GHz outburst detections of 13.6 +/-3.2 and 19.6 +/-4.4 uJy plus one <14.4 uJy epoch; their text reports minute-scale variability/flaring up to 95.0 +/-15.0 uJy. These are state-dependent atmosphere/disk models and should not replace the quiescent value with a single permanent temperature.
